text.p: Following are the main stories in Tuesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- All newspapers lead with Malacca state assemblyman Sahar Arpan claiming trial on three counts of corruption related to applications for two lots of land he allegedly approved.

-- Acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim have asked Rural Development Minister Annuar Musa and Primary Industries Minister Lim Keng Yaik to explain Lim's allegations that 600 million ringgit was missing from a rubber industry development authority.

-- Malaysia's health authorities have posted a bulletin on the Internet to seek help over a baffling disease which has claimed the lives of 14 young children in Sarawak state. The disease is suspected to be caused by the rare Coxsackie virus B.
